speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with hematuria and right flank pain; to begin our evaluation, have you experienced any fever, chills, nausea, or vomiting alongside these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of recurrent urinary tract infections and current symptoms, have you noticed any painless episodes of bright red blood in your urine previously, or does the pain always accompany the bleeding?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Recurrent stone formation leading to ureteral colic and hematuria, likely exacerbated by recurrent UTIs.
